# Syntropy Earth

> Social impact and CSR programme design for organisations already carrying an obligation: a Section 135 CSR mandate, a head-office commitment, a duty-of-care exposure or a BRSR assurance deadline. A brand and growth consultancy practice sits alongside it. Based in Bengaluru, India.

Syntropy Earth is a founder-led advisory practice run by Abhijith Magal, who spent nine years across two global pharmaceutical multinationals before founding it, including brand and commercial work across more than 40 countries, a landmark obesity treatment launch, and health-equity and social responsibility leadership working directly with the WHO-Foundation and UNICEF.

The governing idea is that climate change reaches people first as a health and access problem rather than an environmental one. The sharper operating statement is the completion spine: closing the gap between an entitlement existing and a person actually receiving it. Work attaches to a budget that is already moving rather than to a category, which means mandated CSR spend under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, headquarters duty-of-care mandates, employer duty of care to a workforce, or a BRSR assurance clock.

## The two practices

**Social Impact.** The flagship. CSR programme design under Section 135, health equity and patient access programme design, workforce heat and duty of care, and BRSR assurance readiness. Programmes are built around the company's own mission and designed to survive a board question, an auditor and a change of CSR head. Work usually starts by reading the existing portfolio, because valuable activity is normally already being undercounted or tagged against the wrong goal. Measurement maps to BRSR and GRI. Implementing-partner screening runs to a published standard, and Syntropy Earth takes no money from implementing partners in any form. Design comes first, with implementation and handover behind it.

**Brand and Growth.** Marketing and management consultancy built on nine years of commercial work across global markets. Brand strategy and full brand plans, launch packs from ideation through sales-force effectiveness, operational improvement, cost and financial models, capability centre build-out, and agency orchestration. Priced and delivered as strategy, with an execution partner brought in transparently where execution is required.

**Climate Access Stress Test (CAST).** The scored diagnostic that sits under the social impact practice. Four dimensions, four seasons, one score: geographic exposure, supply chain and operational continuity, workforce availability, and financial and demand continuity, each read across heat, monsoon, air and drought. Includes pathway analysis of how one break cascades into others, and produces disclosure-ready climate-access metrics. CAVS-S is its free, self-serve, directional version.

Explicitly not offered, and referred out: technical ESG, net-zero roadmapping, emissions accounting, and disclosure assurance.

- [Common questions](https://syntropyearth.com/about/questions/): How the practice works, what it costs to start, what it refuses.
- [Unspent CSR Funds Calculator](https://syntropyearth.com/tools/unspent-csr-funds-calculator/): Free Section 135 calculator. Computes the CSR obligation for FY 2026-27 and shows what parks in the Unspent CSR Account and what transfers out.
- [Climate-Access Exposure Scorecard](https://syntropyearth.com/climate-access/): Free self-screen, CAVS-S, about three minutes, benchmarked against FY2024-25 BRSR disclosures from 59 listed Indian companies; an email is asked for at the end to receive the result.
- [Privacy Policy](https://syntropyearth.com/privacy/): What is collected, why, who processes it, and how to have it deleted.

## Thinking (articles)

- [Thinking index](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/): Evidence-led writing on where climate change meets healthcare.
- [The Continuity Cohort Method](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/continuity-cohort-method/): The published method for holding treatment continuity through a disaster response. A named cohort of people on continuous treatment is fixed from government registers at the early action trigger, carried through the response, and reconciled at day twenty-one against the area's own baseline. Method note DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22861246; study protocol DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22880413. Developed by Abhijith Magal, Syntropy Earth.
- [Implementing Partner Screening: IPSS v1.0](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/implementing-partner-screening/): The Implementation Partner Screening Standard, a published method for choosing between eligible CSR implementing organisations under Section 135, with DOIs for the standard (10.5281/zenodo.22814160) and white paper (10.5281/zenodo.22823149).
- [Climate Change Is a Healthcare Story](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/climate-change-is-a-healthcare-story/): The core argument for reading climate as a health and access problem first.
- [Why the Heat Season Is a Healthcare Operations Problem](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/india-heat-season-healthcare-operations/): Extreme heat as a workforce, access and supply-chain problem, not just a medical one.
- [The Climate Risk Hiding in Your Access Data](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/climate-risk-hiding-in-your-access-data/): How seasonal signals of climate disruption already sit in programme data nobody has read that way.
- [The Lancet Countdown 2025, in India's Operating Terms](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/lancet-countdown-2025-india-operating-terms/): What the 2025 findings mean for organisations operating in India.
- [When the HQ Climate-Health Mandate Lands on the India Arm](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/hq-climate-health-mandate-india-arm/): What to do when a global headquarters commitment arrives with a deadline attached.
- [What the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill 2026 changes about Section 135, and what it does not](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/corporate-laws-amendment-bill-2026-section-135/): India-specific. The four proposed changes to Section 135, the Joint Parliamentary Committee's recommendations of 3 August 2026, and how to budget so the allocation holds either way.
- [Assessment or assurance: what SEBI actually changed in BRSR Core](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/brsr-core-assessment-or-assurance-sebi/): India-specific. A provision-by-provision reading of SEBI's 28 March 2025 circular against the July 2023 rule, and what a company now has to hold itself.
- [Air quality is an access problem too. The respiratory story is the half that gets counted](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/air-quality-healthcare-access/): Global argument with India as the worked example. What air pollution evidence measures, the unmeasured loss of routine care during severe episodes, and how to tie a programme calendar to forecast-based emergency stages.
- [CSRD after Omnibus I: which groups still report, and what that asks of a subsidiary outside the EU](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/csrd-omnibus-non-eu-parent-health-disclosure/): Global. Directive (EU) 2026/470 read from the text: the EUR 450 million and 1,000-employee tests, the third-country EUR 450 million and EUR 200 million tests, the revised ESRS of 3 July 2026, and what a subsidiary outside the EU should collect now.
- [Your climate risk assessment found the flood. It did not find the patient](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/physical-risk-versus-access-risk/): Global. A side-by-side comparison of a conventional physical climate risk assessment, aligned to IFRS S2 and TCFD, and an access risk assessment built on the four climate-access conditions, with the three steps that connect them.
- [BRSR, ESRS, GRI, ISSB: which standard asks whether care actually reached anyone?](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/reporting-standards-health-access-coverage/): Global. BRSR, ESRS, GRI 102 and IFRS S2 with SASB compared on one question: whether any requires disclosure of climate-disrupted health access. None does. Includes the voluntary line each structure can carry.
- [When the emergency ends and the access gap does not](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/climate-displacement-continuity-of-care/): Global, for humanitarian and development funders. IDMC 2026 displacement figures, the evidence on chronic care continuity after displacement, the measurement gap, and a register design that counts reconnection.
- [When the clinic has no water](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/water-health-facilities-access/): Global. WHO/UNICEF JMP 2026 estimates for water in health facilities, WHO minimum water quantities as a service cascade, and what a programme should know about partner facilities in the dry season.
- [The cold chain ended at the clinic. The heat did not](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/ambient-heat-medicine-stability-access/): Global. WHO climatic zones and Zone IVb stability conditions, measured storage temperatures after the cold chain, the molecule-specific limits of degradation evidence, and what a programme can monitor.
- [The Lancet Countdown 2026, in operating terms: six India numbers, and the one the sheet does not carry](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/lancet-countdown-2026-india-operating-terms/): India-specific. The 2026 India data sheet read number by number: 4.2 per cent of GDP in lost earnings, 193 billion labour hours with agriculture at 68 per cent, 2,600 heat-stress hours and 64 hours of sleep a year, fossil fuel subsidies at 49 per cent of health spending, and no adaptation indicator.
- [India writes more heat-and-worker research than any country. Nine per cent of it tests a fix.](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/heat-worker-research-india-nine-percent-tests-a-fix/): India-specific. A Harvard mapping review of 210 occupational heat studies in poorer countries: India supplied 30 per cent, 9 per cent tested an intervention, 39 per cent included no women. Why the employer who owns the site is positioned to produce the missing evidence.
- [WHO says USD 24 back per dollar. Health adaptation still gets a third of its bill.](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/who-cop31-health-adaptation-return-per-dollar/): Global, with India as the worked example. WHO's COP31 briefing (1.6 million lives a year, about USD 24 per dollar, the Antalya Initiative for Health Resilience), the Lancet Countdown's adaptation ledger (71 per cent of countries without a plan, USD 3.3 billion needed against 1.1 committed) and ADB's finding that under 1 per cent of adaptation finance targets health.
- [Heat does not kill who you think. The people it kills are on treatment.](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/heat-kills-people-on-treatment/): Global evidence read for an Indian site. Europe's summer 2026 toll (over 50,000, 45 per cent aged 85 or over), India's USD 33.8 billion a year in over-65 heat mortality, a PLOS ONE study showing diabetes and hypertension blunt the autonomic response to heat, and summer cooling poverty. Why daily-medicine status belongs in the heat risk register.
- [20 heat deaths or 359? The alert that never reached the site](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/heatwatch-2026-heat-deaths-alert-reach/): India-specific. HeatWatch's stocktake of the 2026 summer: 359 heat deaths reported against 20 confirmed, 23.4 per cent of deaths medically certified, 63 cooling centres nationwide, and 13.6 per cent of surveyed construction workers in Raipur aware of any heat alert against IMD's 80 per cent reach. The gap between district and gate, and who closes it.
- [Heat and smog used to take turns in Delhi. On 388 days they arrived together.](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/delhi-heat-smog-co-extreme-days/): India-specific. A Hong Kong Baptist University study counts 388 days in Delhi between 2017 and 2024 with extreme heat and severe pollution together, with fine organic carbon up to 2.3 times usual levels. Heat plans and clean air plans sit with different authorities; a site needs one trigger for the day that is both.
- [Measure heat where the child stands: WHO's new indicators and the 2.7 degree gap](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/heat-ready-schools-measure-at-the-site/): Global evidence for an Indian school. WHO, WMO, UNICEF and UNFPA's 19 heat indicators for maternal, newborn and child health (21 October 2026), including school attendance, and a Japanese creche study finding sun-exposed WBGT at child height 2.7 degrees above the official value with shaded ground at 42.8 degrees. What a Heat-Ready Schools sprint measures.
- [Two cyclones, one register: what Andhra Pradesh counted, and the list nobody keeps](https://syntropyearth.com/thinking/cyclone-arnab-murasu-chronic-patient-register/): India-specific. Cyclones Arnab (28 October) and Murasu (3 November 2026): Andhra Pradesh's pre-landfall health inventories, 4,228 pregnant women identified and 3,100 moved, 6,870 listed by due date, 43,672 anti-venom doses, and no count of anyone on daily treatment. Why the maternity register exists and the chronic-care one does not, and how the Continuity Cohort Method builds it.

- [SASB Explained](https://syntropyearth.com/guide/frameworks/sasb.html): Where it lives now.

- [TCFD & ISSB Explained](https://syntropyearth.com/guide/frameworks/tcfd-issb.html): The climate-related financial disclosure lineage.
- [CDP Explained](https://syntropyearth.com/guide/frameworks/cdp.html): How the scoring actually works.
- [The SDGs Explained for Climate-Health](https://syntropyearth.com/guide/frameworks/sdgs.html): Which goals a climate-health programme genuinely maps to.
- [COP History & Global Climate Targets](https://syntropyearth.com/guide/frameworks/cop.html): What each commitment actually binds a country to.
